title: Stripe-based paged-KV + atomic fusion RFC
content:
Goal
------
Sketch an approach for a stripe-oriented paged KV layout that enables: atomic fused reductions during attention compute, cooperative stripe prefetching (to reduce PCIe / NVLink thrash), and a scheduler-side packing heuristic for mixed-length sequences. This is an RFC/notes doc — exploratory, contains code sketches, microbench ideas, and open questions.

Motivation / Problem statement
----------------------------
- Paged KV cache (we page KV shards in/out when context windows exceed local memory) has two recurring costs: (1) transfer latency + PCIe/NVLink throughput when a page is needed, (2) kernel inefficiency when KV blocks don't align with warp-level cooperation patterns.
- When using FlashAttention-like kernels we want to fuse KV loads, softmax/scale, matmul, and the writeback of KV pages into fewer kernel launches. However, naive fusion hurts when pages are fetched async or when only small stripes are used.
- For large multitenant inference workloads we also see mixed length batches: naive big-batch packing forces eviction thrash or leaves many small active ranges that underutilize the device.

Goals
-----
1) Define a stripe layout for paged-KV that: (a) allows partial stripe loads, (b) supports atomic in-place reductions when multiple queries hit same KV stripe concurrently, (c) can be memory-mapped for fast memcpy-to-GPU.
2) Design CUDA kernel primitives that fuse: load-stripe, kv-apply-scale/rotary, flash-attn microtile, and optional writeback, minimizing intermediate global mem traffic.
3) Propose scheduler heuristics to pack requests to maximize stripe reuse and reduce page thrash while preserving latency SLOs.
4) Propose experiments / perf targets and a migration path from current paged-KV implementation.

High-level stripe layout
------------------------
- Stripe = contiguous chunk of KV across sequence dimension and contiguous embed-dimension tiles: basically a rectangular tile (S_stripe x D_tile).
- Each page on disk/network maps to N stripes; a single stripe can be resident independently. Stripe granularity tuned to warp-level co-op size (e.g., 128 tokens x 64 dims) so a warp/block maps to 1..k stripes without divergence.
- Metadata per stripe (in hot GPU mem): stripe_state (RESIDENT / FETCHING / EVICTED), epoch, refcount, pending-writes. Keep small fixed-size header to avoid cacheline thrash.
- Concurrency model: multiple threads/warps can request same stripe. If stripe is RESIDENT, they proceed. If FETCHING, they spin/park on a small ticket lock and then perform cooperative loads when resident. If EVICTED they attempt to install a fetch request; first requester becomes fetch-leader.

Atomic fusion primitives
------------------------
Idea: implement a kernel primitive that accepts a list of stripes to operate on and performs, in one pass, the following pipeline: cooperative stripe load (if required) -> per-tile transform (scale + rotary) -> attention microkernel (FlashAttention inner loop) -> optional accumulate to KV (atomically combine writes) -> release stripe. This reduces round trips and intermediate writes.

Key kernel building blocks (sketches):
- cooperative_prefetch(stripe_id, dst_smem): leader thread posts DMA, other threads park and then map stripe into SMEM when DMA completes. Prefetch returns a tag.
- fused_attention_microtile(q_tile, k_stripe_smem, v_stripe_smem, out_tile): single-kernel microdot that uses reduced-precision accumulators where safe.
- atomic_kv_accumulate(stripe_dst, new_k_tile, new_v_tile): API that atomically merges in updates when we need to writeback sliding windows (used for autoregressive caching in certain configs). We avoid full-page writes by stripe-level CAS + reduction.

Pseudocode (very rough)
-----------------------
__device__ void serve_query(query_t q) {
  list<stripe_id> stripes = compute_needed_stripes(q);
  // schedule stripes by hotness -> resident first
  sort_by_resident_priority(stripes);

  for stripe in stripes {
    tag = cooperative_prefetch(stripe, smem_buf_for_stripe); // DMA launched by leader
    // wait on tag -> then run fused microtile compute
    fused_attention_microtile(q.q_tile, smem.k, smem.v, q.out);
    if (stripe.needs_writeback) atomic_kv_accumulate(stripe.dst, smem.k_out, smem.v_out);
  }
}

Scheduling / packing heuristics (host/runtime)
---------------------------------------------
- At scheduler-level we maintain a small LRU per-GPU for stripe hotness and an occupancy estimator (how many warps are expected to touch each stripe in the current scheduling window).
- When a request arrives with many tokens, we split it into segments and prefer to co-schedule smaller requests that touch the same set of stripes (co-pack) within a micro-batch to reduce duplicate fetches.
- Heuristic (alpha): maximize sum_over_stripes(min(1, usage_count(stripe))) - beta * added_latency. This encourages packing requests that reuse stripes (value 1 per stripe used) while penalizing added latency.
- Admission control: if a request would fetch > M stripes that are cold and would saturate PCIe bandwidth, we either (a) route to lower-tier instance (if possible), (b) degrade by using a smaller KV model variant (quantized), or (c) perform a background prefetch and return a queued response (only for non-SLO-critical paths).

Handling mixed-length sequences
-------------------------------
- Mixed-length sequences are where packing helps the most. We propose: build multi-pass packing:
  1) Bin incoming requests by dominant shard set (approx via hashing first N tokens).
  2) Within bin, greedily pack until marginal stripe reuse falls below threshold.
  3) If a request sits unassigned for >T ms, escalate to solo execution.
- Fast-path: single-request small queries that fit within cache are scheduled immediately (hot cache).

Memory consistency and atomicity concerns
---------------------------------------
- Atomic_kv_accumulate is tricky: we need to maintain semantic correctness for autoregressive cache updates across concurrent requests. Approach: use epoched CAS per stripe header; writers increment epoch and write stripe payload to a staging buffer; final commit atomically swaps pointer and increments epoch again. Readers with older epoch retry or use previous stripe view. We prefer versioning + RCU style semantics over fine-grained per-element locks to avoid high contention.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation
--------------------------------
- If cooperative_prefetch is slow (PCIe saturated), fall back to a lighter-weight kernel that streams KV directly from device memory into compute (no SMEM staging) trading throughput for latency. This fallback reduces bursty PCIe demand.
- If atomic accumulation fails due to contention, fall back to serialized writeback in the host orchestrator (not ideal but safe).

Engineering plan / incremental rollout
-------------------------------------
1) Micro-benchmark: implement stripe layout in CPU-only simulator + measure estimated bandwidth for various stripe sizes (64x64, 128x64, 256x128) using offline traces (collect from prod for 72h).
2) Implement cooperative_prefetch + small SMEM-based fused_attention_microtile kernel (no writeback) — expose as experimental flag on a single GPU pool. Run A/B latency tests.
3) Add atomic_kv_accumulate and epoched stripe headers; run stress tests with concurrent autoregressive writes.
4) Scheduler heuristics: integrate packer into request router; run soak tests with mixed-length synthetic workloads.

Perf targets / experiments
-------------------------
- Target: reduce total bytes transferred over NVLink/PCIe per token by at least 30% for mixed-length workloads with >1 stripe reuse.
- Target: keep 99p tail increase < 10% when enabling stripe fusion for hot workloads vs baseline.
- Benchmarks: single-GPU flash-attention baseline; baseline + stripe-prefetch (SMEM staging); stripe + atomic fusion; stripe + fallback. Measure tokens/sec, p99 latency, and NVLink bytes/sec.

Open questions / risks
---------------------
- Stripe sizing: too small -> too many DMA operations; too large -> SMEM pressure and warp divergence. Need trace-driven tuning.
- Epoched CAS semantics might interact poorly with long-running requests — need to bound epoch churn.
- Interplay with quantized kernels: can we fuse quant-dequant operations cheaply? Should we instead store stripes quantized and dequant in SMEM?
- Debugging complexity: fused large kernels are harder to debug/perf tune. Strategy: build small-stage tests and visibility hooks (tracepoints when fetch starts/ends, counters for stripe reuse).

Notes / TODOs
-------------
- Collect 72h production KV access traces (Ana) -> bucket by stripe candidates.
- Run offline simulator for stripe sizes (Marcus).
- Prototype cooperative_prefetch skeleton (Kenji) and land PR with feature flag: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Add scheduler packing PoC in router (experiment namespace).

References / background reading
-----------------------------
- FlashAttention paper + implementations (benchmark against ours)
- Prior paged-KV work inside serving runtime (see existing docs in drive)
- RCU / epoched data structure patterns for lock-free readers

Appendix: small kernel sketch (pseudo-CUDA)
------------------------------------------
// very rough pseudocode to capture intent
__global__ void fused_prefetch_attention_kernel(query_t* queries, stripe_meta_t* meta) {
  int qid = blockIdx.x;
  query_t q = queries[qid];
  stripe_id s = q.primary_stripe;
  if (threadIdx.x==0) {
    if (atomicCAS(&meta[s].state, EVICTED, FETCHING) == EVICTED) {
      // leader posts async copy (cudaMemcpyAsync) into device buffer and flips state->RESIDENT when done
      post_dma(meta[s].device_ptr, meta[s].host_ptr, meta[s].size);
    }
  }
  __syncthreads(); // naive barrier; real impl uses tag/waitlist
  // now run fused microtile on smem copy or directly on device_ptr
  fused_attention_microtile(...);
  if (q.needs_update) atomic_kv_accumulate(...);
}

Closing
-------
This is intentionally exploratory. The stripe+atomic-fusion approach trades implementation complexity for substantial reductions in interconnect traffic and fewer kernel-launch overheads. Next step: run trace-driven simulation to pick stripe-size sweet spots and prototype cooperative_prefetch with a minimal fused microtile to measure real SMEM vs DRAM latency tradeoffs.
